key_insight: Preparing permutation-symmetric Dicke states via local measurements and feedback maps exactly to a classical first-passage process that transports and absorbs singlet-pair constraint violations.
engineering_relevance: The mapping replaces exponentially large many-body dynamics with a polynomial-size generator for analyzing preparation speed, feedback geometry, robustness, and fluctuations.
method: Detect violations of permutation symmetry using local singlet projectors.
Close the dynamics exactly on N_q(N_q−1)/2 pair projectors, with measurements moving endpoints and feedback absorbing pairs.
Use additional exact closures to determine final states and ensemble fluctuations.
evidence_signal: Analytical results include the exact one-dimensional Liouvillian eigenvalue 2[1−cos(π/N_q)] in measurement-rate units and an at-least-linear relaxation-time bound for local feedback; the abstract reports no hardware evaluation.
watch_item: Exact solvability does not imply fast preparation: the reported one-dimensional eigenvalue scales as N_q⁻², implying a quadratic slow relaxation timescale.
paper_title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
